prompt: Rewrite as a cleft sentence with <It was ... who>
source: Maria organized the whole event.
correct: It was Maria who organized the whole event.
explanation: Cleft with <It was ... who> emphasizes the agent (person).

prompt: Rewrite as a cleft sentence with <It was ... that>
source: The heavy rain caused the flooding.
correct: It was the heavy rain that caused the flooding.
explanation: Cleft with <It was ... that> emphasizes the cause.

source: I admire her courage.
correct: What I admire is her courage.
What I admire about her is her courage.
explanation: <What> cleft: <What> + subject + verb + <is> + focused element.

source: He resigned immediately.
correct: What he did was resign immediately.
What he did was to resign immediately.
hint: After <What ... did was>, use base form or <to> + infinitive
explanation: <What ... did was> + base verb/to-infinitive focuses on the action.

prompt: Rewrite as a cleft sentence with <It is ... where>
source: They met at a conference in Berlin.
correct: It was at a conference in Berlin where they met.
It was in Berlin where they met at a conference.
explanation: Cleft with <It was ... where> emphasizes the location.

source: He quit because the salary was too low.
correct: The reason he quit is that the salary was too low.
The reason why he quit is that the salary was too low.
explanation: <The reason (why) ... is that> focuses on the cause/motivation.

source: The country needs economic reform.
correct: What the country needs is economic reform.
explanation: <What ... needs is> cleft emphasizes the required solution.

prompt: Rewrite as a cleft sentence with <It was ... when>
source: I realized the mistake only after submitting the report.
correct: It was only after submitting the report that I realized the mistake.
It was after submitting the report when I realized the mistake.
explanation: Cleft with time focus: <It was ... that/when> emphasizes timing.

source: The system crashed and we lost all the data.
correct: What happened was that the system crashed and we lost all the data.
What happened was the system crashed and we lost all the data.
explanation: <What happened was (that)> introduces an explanation of events.

source: I just want a quiet evening at home.
correct: All I want is a quiet evening at home.
explanation: <All ... is> cleft minimizes and focuses: <the only thing I want is>.

source: His arrogance bothers me most.
correct: The thing that bothers me most is his arrogance.
explanation: <The thing that ... is> defers the focus element to the end.

prompt: Rewrite as a cleft with <It is ... who>
source: You should apologize, not me.
correct: It is you who should apologize, not me.
explanation: Cleft for contrast: <It is you who> emphasizes the responsible person.

source: The plot twist made the film memorable.
correct: What made the film memorable was the plot twist.
explanation: <What made X [adjective] was Y> focuses on the cause of a quality.

source: The CEO approved the merger.
correct: The person who approved the merger was the CEO.
explanation: <The person/thing who/that ... was> pseudo-cleft defers focus to the end.

prompt: Rewrite using <It was not until ... that>
source: She didn't understand the problem until she read the report.
correct: It was not until she read the report that she understood the problem.
It wasn't until she read the report that she understood the problem.
explanation: <It was not until ... that> emphasizes lateness or delay.

source: I grew up in a small village by the sea.
correct: Where I grew up is a small village by the sea.
Where I grew up was a small village by the sea.
explanation: <Where ... is> pseudo-cleft focuses on a place.

prompt: Rewrite using <What ... is> with abstract focus
source: We lack proper communication.
correct: What we lack is proper communication.
explanation: <What we lack/need/want is> focuses on what is missing.

prompt: Rewrite as a cleft with <It is ... that> (negative)
source: Money doesn't make you happy.
correct: It is not money that makes you happy.
It isn't money that makes you happy.
explanation: Negative cleft: <It is not X that ...> denies a cause/factor.

source: She handled the crisis brilliantly.
correct: The way she handled the crisis was brilliant.
explanation: <The way ... is/was> + adjective focuses on manner.

source: They should invest in renewable energy.
correct: What they should do is invest in renewable energy.
explanation: <What ... should do is> + base verb focuses on the recommended action.

prompt: Rewrite as a cleft with focus on the object
source: I bought the blue dress, not the red one.
correct: It was the blue dress that I bought, not the red one.
explanation: Cleft focusing on the object: <It was [object] that I [verb]>.

source: We first met at the university library.
correct: The place where we first met was the university library.
explanation: <The place where ... was> pseudo-cleft focuses on location.

source: He only smiled and walked away.
correct: All he did was smile and walk away.
explanation: <All ... did was> + base verb emphasizes the simplicity/minimality of the action.

prompt: Rewrite using <It was because of ... that>
source: His hard work got him promoted.
correct: It was because of his hard work that he got promoted.
explanation: <It was because of ... that> cleft focuses on the reason.

source: The employees want better working conditions.
correct: What the employees want is better working conditions.
explanation: <What ... want is> pseudo-cleft focuses on the desired outcome.
